stem.text: A $0.80\,\text{m}$ length of steel wire and a $1.4\,\text{m}$ length of brass wire are joined together. The combined wires are suspended from a fixed support and a force of $40\,\text{N}$ is applied, as shown.

stem.alt: Diagram of two wires joined end to end and hung from a fixed support, with the upper section labelled steel and the lower section labelled brass, and a downward force of 40 N applied at the bottom.

stem.text: The Young modulus of steel is $2.0 \times 10^{11}\,\text{Pa}$.
The Young modulus of brass is $1.0 \times 10^{11}\,\text{Pa}$.
Each wire has a cross-sectional area of $2.4 \times 10^{-6}\,\text{m}^{2}$.
What is the total extension? Ignore the weights of the wires.
